title: SQLite
subtitle: SQLite gives each of FAFOHive's social and media modules durable, transactional state that one process owns.
lede: FAFOHive's in-house social modules each need durable, transactional state owned by one process, and I gave each its own SQLite database. Where one process owns the state, most concurrency turns into ordinary transactions. The X module keeps a work queue in SQLite and claims jobs inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions, which take the write lock up front, so two workers never claim the same job after a scheduler restart. The Facebook module keeps an inventory of every object it creates, which gives cleanup and reconciliation an exact list. The Reddit module stores a receipt for every change and an archive of every response it reads, so a repeated request with the same idempotency key returns the first receipt.
quote: I pick the smallest storage that gives a component its guarantee, and I design around the moment between sent and confirmed.
evidence: Embedded database design with SQLite: one database per process-owned module, so work-queue claims, object inventories and idempotent receipts are ordinary transactions.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: render-job identity written before sending, and an explicit outcome-unknown state settled by reading the renderer at startup, never resubmitted.
author: Corey James
